comments.text:
Note that when speaking of what somebody else wants you should use the -がる form. E.g. たい→たがる. Basically you shouldn't say "She wants to ___" but "She looks like she wants to ___".

In asking questions the direct 〜たい form is fine.

comments.text: In modern Japanese 〜たい generally takes を with が being used for emphasis when strong feelings are involved.

comments.text: From what I've heard (and seen used), 〜たい / 〜ほしい is used even when referring to other people, because it's regarded more polite than 〜がる forms. This might be limited only to 2nd person, though, I'm not completely sure.
